results.title: Algebra maps from an étale DVR extension into a Henselian one match residue-field maps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ finite $A$-algebras whose structure maps are local homomorphisms, $B$ étale over $A$, and $C$ a Henselian local ring. Write $\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. Then sending an $A$-algebra homomorphism $B \to C$ to the $\kappa(A)$-algebra homomorphism $\kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ it induces is a bijection.

results.title: Holomorphic functions on open subsets of ℂⁿ have continuous derivative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $s$ be an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$ and let $f : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be complex differentiable at every point of $s$. Then the complex derivative $x \mapsto Df(x)$, with values in the complex linear maps $\mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$, is continuous on $s$. Here $\mathbb{C}^n$ carries the Euclidean norm.

results.title: Vanishing of the Wirtinger derivative at points of complex differentiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. If $f$ is complex differentiable at $z$, then the Wirtinger derivative $\partial f / \partial \bar z$ of $f$ vanishes at $z$.

results.title: Cauchy–Riemann criterion for complex differentiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. If $f$ is real differentiable at $z$ and its Wirtinger derivative $\partial f / \partial \bar z$ vanishes at $z$, then $f$ is complex differentiable at $z$.

results.title: Solving the ∂̄-equation for compactly supported C¹ data
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be real differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous real derivative and compact support. Then there is a function $u : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, real differentiable on all of $\mathbb{C}$, whose Wirtinger derivative satisfies $\frac{\partial u}{\partial \bar z}(z) = g(z)$ for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Hartogs extension theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n$ be open and connected, and let $K \subseteq U$ be compact with $U \setminus K$ connected. Then for every function $f : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic on $U \setminus K$ there is a function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic on $U$ and agrees with $f$ on $U \setminus K$. Here $\mathbb{C}^n$ carries the Euclidean norm.

results.title: Partial derivative along a coordinate axis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a coordinate index $i$, let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector. The partial derivative $\partial_i f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ sends $x$ to the derivative at $t = 0$ of $t \mapsto f(x + t e_i)$, taken to be $0$ when this function is not differentiable at $0$.

results.title: Partial derivative as the derivative of a coordinate slice
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, a coordinate index $i$ and a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector. The partial derivative of $f$ along the $i$-th coordinate axis at $x$ equals the derivative at $t = 0$ of the one-variable function $t \mapsto f(x + t e_i)$, taken to be $0$ when that function is not differentiable at $0$.

results.title: Partial derivative as a Fréchet derivative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at a point $x$, and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the partial derivative of $f$ along the $i$-th coordinate axis at $x$ equals $Df(x)\,e_i$, the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ applied to $e_i$.

results.title: Partial derivative function of a differentiable function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable and let $e_i$ be the $i$-th standard basis vector of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then the partial derivative $\partial_i f$ of $f$ along the $i$-th coordinate axis is the function $x \mapsto Df(x)\,e_i$, where $Df(x)$ is the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$.

results.title: Symmetry of mixed partial derivatives (Clairaut's theorem)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a function $g : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, write $\partial_i g$ for its partial derivative along the $i$-th coordinate axis. If $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is twice continuously differentiable, then for all coordinate indices $i, j$ and every point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $\partial_j (\partial_i f)(x) = \partial_i (\partial_j f)(x)$.

results.title: Polar of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space. The polar of a set $A \subseteq E$ is the set $A^\circ = \{y \in E : \langle x, y \rangle \le 1 \text{ for all } x \in A\}$. This uses the one-sided bound $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$, not $|\langle x, y \rangle| \le 1$.

results.title: Membership in the polar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space, $A \subseteq E$ and $y \in E$. Then $y$ lies in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$ if and only if $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$ for every $x \in A$.

results.title: Polar of the empty set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a real inner product space $E$, the polar of the empty set is all of $E$, since the defining condition is vacuous.

results.title: The origin lies in every polar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a real inner product space $E$, for every set $A \subseteq E$ the origin $0$ lies in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$, since $\langle x, 0 \rangle = 0 \le 1$ for every $x \in A$.

results.title: The polar reverses inclusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of a real inner product space. If $A \subseteq B$, then the polar $B^\circ$ of $B$ is contained in the polar $A^\circ$ of $A$.

results.title: The closed unit ball is self-polar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a real inner product space $E$, the polar of the closed unit ball $\{x \in E : \|x\| \le 1\}$ is the closed unit ball itself.

results.title: The polar of the cube is the $\ell^1$ unit ball
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the polar of the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is the set of all $y$ with $\langle x, y \rangle \le 1$ for every $x$ in the cube, is the closed $\ell^1$ unit ball $\{y \in \mathbb{R}^n : \sum_i |y_i| \le 1\}$.

results.title: Polar of a linear image
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, let $f : E \to F$ be a linear map with adjoint $f^* : F \to E$, and let $K \subseteq E$. Writing $S^\circ$ for the polar of a set $S$, we have $(f(K))^\circ = (f^*)^{-1}(K^\circ)$, that is, $y \in F$ lies in the polar of $f(K)$ if and only if $f^*(y)$ lies in the polar of $K$.

results.title: Hypersequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in an additive commutative monoid. Its hypersequence of generation $r$, written $a^{(r)}_n$, is defined by recursion on $r$: $a^{(0)}_n = a_n$ and $a^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a^{(r)}_k$ for all natural numbers $r$ and $n$. Thus each generation is the sequence of partial sums of the previous one.

results.title: Each hypersequence generation sums the previous one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence in an additive commutative monoid and let $a^{(r)}_n$ denote its hypersequence of generation $r$. For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, $a^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a^{(r)}_k$.

results.title: First hypersequence at index zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence in an additive commutative monoid and let $a^{(1)}_n$ denote its hypersequence of generation $1$. Then $a^{(1)}_0 = a_0$.

results.title: Hyperfibonacci numbers are the hypersequences of the Fibonacci numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F_k$ denote the $k$th Fibonacci number. For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the hyperfibonacci number $F^{(r)}_n$ equals the $r$th hypersequence of the Fibonacci sequence at $n$, that is, $F^{(r)}_n = a^{(r)}_n$ for $a_k = F_k$, where $a^{(0)}_n = a_n$ and $a^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a^{(r)}_k$.

results.title: Bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instance is a pair $(n, \varphi)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of variables, and a CNF formula $\varphi$.

results.title: Well-formed bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$ is well formed when every clause of $\varphi$ is a list of exactly three literals, not necessarily distinct, every literal of $\varphi$ has a variable less than $n$, and for every variable $v < n$ at most four of the literals in the clauses of $\varphi$, counted with multiplicity and with either polarity, have variable $v$.

results.title: Satisfiable bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$ is satisfiable when there is a list $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of booleans such that $\varphi$ is satisfied by the assignment sending each variable $x < n$ to $a_x$ and every variable $x \ge n$ to false.

results.title: 3-SAT with bounded occurrences as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem 3-SAT WITH BOUNDED OCCURRENCES accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of bounded-occurrence 3-SAT instances, to an instance that is well formed and satisfiable; it rejects every other bitstring, including every bitstring that does not decode.

results.title: 3-SAT WITH BOUNDED OCCURRENCES is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem 3-SAT WITH BOUNDED OCCURRENCES over bitstrings belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.

results.title: Closest-string instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A closest-string instance is a pair $(S, d)$ of a finite list $S$ of bitstrings (finite lists of booleans) and a natural number $d$, the distance bound.

results.title: Well-formed closest-string instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A closest-string instance $(S, d)$ is well formed when all bitstrings in the list $S$ have the same length.

results.title: Feasible closest-string instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $\ell(x)$ for the length of a bitstring $x$. A closest-string instance $(S, d)$ is feasible when there is a bitstring $c$ with $\ell(c) = \ell(s_1)$, where $s_1$ is the first bitstring of $S$ (and $\ell(c) = 0$ if $S$ is empty), such that for every $s$ in $S$ the number of positions $j < \min(\ell(c), \ell(s))$ at which $c$ and $s$ differ is at most $d$.

results.title: The CLOSEST STRING decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem CLOSEST STRING accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of closest-string instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to a closest-string instance are rejected.

results.title: CLOSEST STRING is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The CLOSEST STRING decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
